source: Whisnant AW et al. (2020) Integrative functional genomics decodes herpes simplex virus 1. Nat Commun 11:2038. PMC7184758, full text read 13 November 2026. Intervals are TRL and TRS, the two terminal repeats. An earlier version of this row encoded TRL and IRL, which is both copies of the long repeat and neither of the short, and is impossible: masking both copies leaves nothing for the paper's own restoration step to copy from. The paper prints no coordinates, so the TRL/TRS identification is an inference from its text and from its own annotation, in which the IRS and TRS features mirror each other exactly.
quote: The HSV-1 genome consists of two components (L and S) that are both flanked by long repeats. To mitigate the effect of multi-mapping reads, we masked the terminal repeats by NNN. ... Finally, all read mappings in the repeats were copied into the previously masked regions.

source: Morse AM et al. (2017) Reconciling Herpes Simplex Virus 1 genomic variation. Viruses 9(8):226. PMC5580483, full text read at pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov on 13 November 2026. The paper states 152,261 bp, which is NC_001806.1, not the .2 used everywhere else here. The two versions differ by 39 bp and the offset between them is NOT constant: 0 near the start, -1 through UL and IRL, -3 to -5 near IRS, and +39 through most of TRS. The intervals recorded here are the .2 equivalents derived in review, and the removed IRL block stops before the 399 bp a' sequence, which belongs to the IRS block Morse kept. Because no crosswalk between the two reference versions exists in this repository, this row was refused outright until the version crosswalk was built (M6). It is now translated through that crosswalk, and every answer about it states the offset applied.
